headline: WikiLeaks Reveals US Spying on Brazilian Officials Ahead of Meeting Between Presidents Obama and Rousseff
subheadline: New Evidence Emerges From Wikileaks and Intercept Journalists
content: WikiLeaks and journalists from The Intercept revealed fresh evidence showing how the American National Security Agency spied upon members of President Dilma Rousseff’s cabinet including Brazil's Foreign Affairs minister Antônio Patriota among others during meetings related to aircraft purchases between Boeing and Embraer involving discussions about ‘OBAMA-ROUSEPPFF’. These revelations come shortly before a meeting scheduled between presidents Obama and Rousseff where both aimed to move past previous tensions caused by earlier leaks confirming surveillance activities against Rousseff herself and Brazilians generally conducted by the NSA leading to cancellation of Rousseff’s visit to Washington planned towards end of last year causing bilateral relations chill.

headline: Greece Faces Divided Nation Over Referendum Decision Today

content: Greek premier Alexis Tsipras warns his nation today over referendum decision which could mark significant turning point in history. Citizens face choice between rejecting harsh austerity measures proposed by Berlin-led European institutions versus accepting bailout terms deemed unsustainable according to government officials who argue voting yes would mean humiliation orchestrated through economic terrorism tactics employed by creditors namely IMF ECB along with other Eurozone entities after failure reaching agreement extending financial aid beyond June 30th prompting temporary bank closures until July 6th amidst ongoing political turmoil within Greece itself.
